published.name: Burnt Orange
published.description:
Set within Sydney Harbour National Park on Middle Head, this Mosman venue occupies a heritage clubhouse built in the 1920s for the Mosman Golf Club. The building has been preserved as a standalone space, with a wrap-around balcony that looks out through native bushland to glimpses of Sydney Harbour.

Open Wednesday to Sunday from 8.30am, it serves breakfast, lunch and a high tea of house-made sweet and savoury bites and freshly baked scones with jam and cream, alongside seasonal dishes. The Signals Room, private dining room and main balcony host weddings, celebrations and events, with the whole venue available for exclusive hire.

published.name: Pinocchio's
published.description: An Italian and seafood restaurant on Railway Parade, working from handcrafted pasta and pizza dough, house-simmered sauces and fresh Australian seafood. Wood-fired pizza is the signature, running from the Napoletana with anchovies and basil to the Jiminy with prosciutto, rocket and shaved parmesan, and Geppetto's with pesto chicken and buffalo mozzarella. Alongside the pizzas the menu takes in pasta and side dishes drawn from Mediterranean cooking. The venue is fully licensed, with no BYO, and larger parties are handled by phone booking.
published.meritSplit: local: Generic Italian-seafood restaurant with standard menu and no distinctive maker, story, or identity beyond typical pizza-pasta offerings.

published.name: Bosk
published.description:
Named for a small wooded area, this restaurant sits among the trees of Clontarf Reserve, on the water in Sydney's suburbs. The menu shifts with the seasons to draw on the freshest produce, so listed ingredients read as a guide to the kitchen's style rather than fixed dishes. It is fully licensed, with seasonally updated cocktails alongside Australian and imported wines and beers.

Breakfast runs Saturday and Sunday from 8am to 11am, and lunch Thursday to Sunday from midday. Group menus cater for gatherings of 10 to 30 adults, with an à la carte and kids menu for smaller tables.

published.name: Moksha
published.description: An Indian restaurant in Jannali that has served its regulars for 18 years, with à la carte and banquet menus. It is BYO. The kitchen sets out to bring Indian food in welcoming surrounds.

published.name: Room two ten
published.description:
Open since 2014, this cafe and bar sits in Freshwater Village. Former owner Steve named it after hostel room #210 from his travels, a nod to his mates and the memories they made, and built the place around low-key hospitality and warmth. In 2023 he handed the keys to Jag and Sosso, who carry on the tradition.

Breakfast and lunch are served seven days a week: familiar dishes revisited with a bit of personality. At heart it's a spot for friends, family, locals and visitors to share a meal, a drink and a story.
published.meritSplit: local: Generic all-day cafe serving familiar dishes with no distinctive identity beyond a friendly backstory.

published.name: Palm Beach Farmers' Market
published.description: Held each Saturday morning, from 6am to 11:30am, in the grounds of Palm Beach Currumbin State High School on Thrower Drive. Stalls run to fresh produce and prepared food, with microgreens and sweets among what turns up. The market is run by The Market Co. GC. Under City of Gold Coast regulations, dogs are not permitted where food is prepared or stored.
softenedClaims: Palm Beach Currumbin State High School on Thrower Drive

published.name: Malaya Corner
published.description:
Malaysian street food served from two Brisbane locations: one in Sunnybank at Shop 38, 341 Mains Rd, the other in Bowen Hills at Shop 3, 2 King Street. The kitchen draws on the hawker stalls of Penang and the kopitiam culture of KL, cooking with fragrant spices, rich curries and noodle soups.

The menu runs to Bak Kut Teh, a herbal soup with pork ribs served with deep-fried bread stick and rice, alongside Penang Lobak, Penang Char Kway Teow, Dry Curry Mee and Malaysian Laksa. A vegetable laksa comes with Hokkien noodles and vermicelli, bean sprouts, broccoli, mushroom, fungus and tofu puff in curry soup.
published.meritSplit: chain: Two-location Brisbane operation with identical branding, franchise-style 'Two Stores, One Flavour' presence — a small chain rather than a single independent venue.
softenedClaims: Dry Curry Mee and Malaysian Laksa

published.name: Hugos
published.description:
On Manly Wharf, this restaurant has served locals and visitors for over 15 years. You can step off the sand into the bar or settle on the deck for a sunset dinner, watching the water while you eat.

The menu leans Mediterranean and seafood-focused: Sydney rock oysters with vermouth eschalot vinaigrette, kingfish carpaccio, spanner crab spaghettini and crispy skin barramundi, alongside pizzas topped with everything from fig and pancetta to slow-roasted lamb. Steaks run to Wagyu scotch fillet, and a cheese board rounds out the list. Playful cocktails and timeless décor set the tone.

published.name: LarryPost
published.description: A stationery and art-supply shop specialising in pens and the tools that go with them. Fountain pens, dip pens, calligraphy nibs and brush pens sit alongside bottled inks, notebooks and journals, watercolours, pencils and paper, drawn from brands including Lamy, Pilot, Sailor, Kaweco, Leuchtturm1917, Faber-Castell and Schmincke. Nibs are checked before they leave the store, and services extend to name debossing and pen repair parts.
published.meritSplit: visitable: Online-only stationery retailer with international currency options and no publicly visitable storefront experience.

published.name: He She La
published.description: A Newari khaja ghar serving Nepalese food, the Hurstville outlet sits on Forest Road near the shopping strip. It shares its menu with the flagship in Rockdale: the Nanglo Set, a Newari feast served on a nanglo tray; Jhol Momo, dumplings in broth; the sweet Yomari Set; and the Heshela Special Thali. Cooking follows traditional recipes with veg and non-veg options, in share-style portions suited to family meals and group gatherings. Open daily, noon to 10pm, with catering for events.
published.meritSplit: chain: Operates two outlets (Rockdale flagship and Hurstville), making it a small local chain by Atlas rules rather than a single independent venue.

published.name: The Oriana
published.description:
A privately owned penthouse apartment on Balmoral Beach, 8 km from Sydney's central business district. The garden runs onto the sand, and the apartment holds 270-degree views along the beach, across the harbour and through Sydney Heads. It has a master bedroom, second and third bedrooms, a reading room and a lounge room facing the beach, with a balcony overlooking the water.

Bathers Pavilion is a minute's walk away, with Ormeggio at the Spit, the Public Dining Room and Mosman's shops nearby. A park adjoins the property, and Taronga Zoo and Manly beach are close.
published.meritSplit: visitable: A single private penthouse holiday rental — a supply of rooms with no distinct visitable identity of its own.

published.name: Angelo's Cabarita
published.description: Set inside Prince Edward Park, at the bay end of Phillips Street on the Cabarita waterfront, this restaurant looks out over the Parramatta River. The kitchen works across Italian, seafood and modern Australian cooking, with à la carte and chef's menus, handmade pasta, fresh seafood and steaks. Lunch and dinner run Wednesday to Sunday, and a private dining room seats up to 14. From Wednesday to Friday, a midweek lunch offer pairs any pasta with house wine and dessert for $49.

published.name: Edmonds and Greer
published.description:
A café and homewares store combined under one roof on Mulga Road in Oatley. The kitchen runs breakfast, brunch and lunch, and the venue also puts on high tea, including a version for children, alongside offsite catering and functions.

Alongside the tables, the shop stocks homewares, fashion and gifts: ceramics and vases, candles and diffusers from Glasshouse, Frank Green bottles and cups, jewellery, bags and wallets, plus gourmet kitchen goods such as Ogilvie & Co preserves. The café serves seven days; the homewares section keeps its own hours.

published.name: Stoneage Korean BBQ
published.description: Korean barbecue on Forest Road in Hurstville, with grills set into the centre of each table and smoke ventilation above them. The staff cook the meats for you, refilling the side dishes as you go. Cuts run to marinated pork ribs and pork belly alongside marinated beef, and the wider menu takes in octopus bibimbap, steam egg stew, shallot salad and a spicy tofu seafood soup. The room is modern and set up for groups, with cash payment earning a discount.

published.name: The Harvest Ground
published.description: Modern Australian cuisine in Penshurst, run by head chef Brendon Baxter, who brings over 13 years of experience and a passion for cooking on an open flame. The menu draws on fresh, local produce, with dishes served across breakfast, lunch and dinner, plus a kids menu and Sunday brunch. The kitchen works with organic ingredients, and the venue is fully licensed.
